title: Unramified algebra maps descend along directed colimits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and let $A=\varinjlim_{i\in I}A_i$ be a directed colimit of commutative rings. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a map of $A_{i_0}$-algebras $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$. For $i\ge i_0$ put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$, $C_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$, and $B=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$. Assume that $B\to C$ is unramified as a ring map, meaning that $C$ is a finitely generated $B$-algebra and its module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{C/B}$ is zero [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and assume that $C_0$ is a finitely generated $B_0$-algebra. Then there exists $i\ge i_0$ such that $B_i\to C_i$ is unramified: $C_i$ is finitely generated over $B_i$ and $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}=0$.

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ of $C_0$ over $B_0$, allowing $m=0$, and write $x_{r,i}=1\otimes x_r\in C_i$. For $i\ge i_0$, every element of $C_i$ is a finite sum of tensors $a\otimes c$. Write $c$ as a polynomial in the $x_r$ with coefficients in $B_0$. Then $a\otimes c$ is the same polynomial in the $x_{r,i}$, with each coefficient $b$ replaced by $a\otimes b\in B_i$ (distribute the scalar $a$ across the coefficients). Thus the $x_{r,i}$ generate $C_i$ over $B_i$. The identical computation with $A$ gives generators of $C$ over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), proof: choose algebra generators; tensor expansion

proof.text: Set $M_0=\Omega_{C_0/B_0}$ and $v_r=\mathrm d x_r$. The presentation in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] says that differentials $\mathrm d c$ generate $M_0$. For a monomial $b x_1^{e_1}\cdots x_m^{e_m}$, repeated Leibniz gives $\mathrm d(b x_1^{e_1}\cdots x_m^{e_m})=\sum_{r:e_r>0} e_r b x_1^{e_1}\cdots x_r^{e_r-1}\cdots x_m^{e_m}\mathrm d x_r$, since $\mathrm d b=0$. Additivity extends this to every polynomial expression for $c$. Hence the $v_r$ generate $M_0$. Applied to the generators from step 1, the same calculation shows that $\mathrm d x_{r,i}$ generate $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}$ for every $i\ge i_0$. If $m=0$, all these modules are zero.

source.place: Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), first generator sentence; the Leibniz calculation in Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), first proof paragraph

proof.text: For any $A_{i_0}$-algebra $T$ put $B_T=T\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$ and $C_T=T\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$. The ring map $B_T\otimes_{B_0}C_0\to C_T$, $(t\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto t\otimes\varphi_0(b)c$, has inverse $t\otimes c\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes c$. The balancing relations verify both composites on pure tensors. Also $C_T\otimes_{C_0}M_0\cong T\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$: send $(t\otimes c)\otimes\omega$ to $t\otimes c\omega$, with inverse $t\otimes\omega\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes\omega$. Again balancing verifies the formulas and their inverse identities. These identifications apply to $T=A_i$ and to $T=A$.

source.place: Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), base-changed rings in the proof; explicit tensor identifications for applying Tag 00RV

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] to $B_0\to B_T$ and $B_0\to C_0$, using the ring identification of step 3. Its $C_T$-module form gives $\Omega_{C_T/B_T}\cong C_T\otimes_{C_0}M_0$. Combining with step 3 gives an isomorphism $F_T:T\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0\longrightarrow\Omega_{C_T/B_T}$ that sends $1\otimes v_r$ to $\mathrm d(1\otimes x_r)$. This generator formula follows from the stated formula for the canonical base-change map. In particular $F_A(1\otimes v_r)=0$, because the hypothesis that $B\to C$ is unramified includes $\Omega_{C/B}=0$. Injectivity of $F_A$ implies $1\otimes v_r=0$ in $A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$ for every $r$.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change); Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), vanishing in the colimit

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] with initial index $i_0$ and the arbitrary $A_{i_0}$-module $M_0$. For each $r$ apply it to $1\otimes v_r\in A_{i_0}\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$: step 4 says its image in $A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$ is zero. Obtain $j_r\ge i_0$ with $1\otimes v_r=0$ in $A_{j_r}\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$. Choose $i\ge i_0,j_1,\ldots,j_m$ by finitely many applications of directedness (take $i=i_0$ if $m=0$). The transition map sends $a\otimes\omega$ to $\alpha_{i j_r}(a)\otimes\omega$, so it sends these zero elements to $1\otimes v_r=0$ in $A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$. Applying $F_{A_i}$ from step 4 yields $\mathrm d x_{r,i}=0$ for every $r$.

source.place: Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), final sentence; Tags 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit) and 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits) for the existing elementwise tensor-colimit lemma

proof.text: At the index $i$ of step 5, every generator $\mathrm d x_{r,i}$ of $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}$ from step 2 is zero; a linear combination of zero generators is zero, so $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}=0$. Step 1 already proves that $C_i$ is a finitely generated $B_i$-algebra. These are exactly the two conditions defining unramified in the statement, and $i\ge i_0$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unramified_stage_of_colimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [HasColimit F] (i₀ : I) (B₀ : Type v) (C₀ : Type w) [CommRing B₀] [CommRing C₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) B₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) C₀] (φ₀ : B₀ →ₐ[F.obj i₀] C₀) (hfg : φ₀.toRingHom.FiniteType) (hunramified : letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) ↥(colimit F) := (colimit.ι F i₀).hom.toAlgebra (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) ↥(colimit F)) φ₀).toRingHom.FiniteType ∧ Subsingleton (@KaehlerDifferential (↥(colimit F) ⊗[F.obj i₀] B₀) (↥(colimit F) ⊗[F.obj i₀] C₀) _ _ (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) ↥(colimit F)) φ₀).toRingHom.toAlgebra)) : ∃ (i : I) (h : i₀ ≤ i), letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i)) φ₀).toRingHom.FiniteType ∧ Subsingleton (@KaehlerDifferential ((F.obj i) ⊗[F.obj i₀] B₀) ((F.obj i) ⊗[F.obj i₀] C₀) _ _ (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i)) φ₀).toRingHom.toAlgebra)
